seo_title: Delhi HC: GPA Holder Must Account for Sale Money
title: Delhi High Court Holds a General Power of Attorney Does Not Transfer Title, Holder Must Account for Full Sale Proceeds
case_name: Bhisham Mehta v. Gita Vig & Ors.
card_summary: Bhisham Mehta, holding a GPA for his sister-in-law Kusum Mehta and other co-owners, sold their jointly owned land for about Rs 6.95 crore but sent her only about Rs 72 lakh. After her death her daughters sued for the balance. The Delhi High Court dismissed his appeal, holding a GPA is only an agency document, never a transfer of ownership, so the holder must account for the full sale proceeds.
card_tip: A GPA used to sell jointly owned property, common where an NRI co-owner cannot be present, never lets the holder keep part of the proceeds; the full amount belongs to the principal and must be accounted for.
verification_notes: The core facts, the agricultural land sale for roughly Rs 6.95 crore, the remittance of only about Rs 72 lakh to Kusum Mehta, the trial court's decree of roughly Rs 1.02 crore with 8% interest, and the holding that a GPA does not transfer title and binds the agent to account for sale proceeds, are reported consistently by LiveLaw, Verdictum and Court Book. Verdictum carries the neutral citation 2026:DHC:7295. Sources differ by a day on the decision date (31 August 2026 in some reports, 1 September 2026 in others); this card uses the earlier date and flags the discrepancy rather than asserting either as certain.
